**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature


**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This makes it simple to see how much huge page memory is in use.

E.g.
```
Allocated resources:                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  (Total limits may be over 100 percent, i.e., overcommitted.)                                                                                                                                                                               
  Resource           Requests     Limits                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  --------           --------     ------
  cpu                850m (85%)   100m (10%)
  memory             191Mi (11%)  390Mi (22%)
  ephemeral-storage  0 (0%)       0 (0%)
  hugepages-1Gi      0 (0%)       0 (0%)
  hugepages-2Mi      6Mi (60%)    6Mi (60%)
  hugepages-32Mi     0 (0%)       0 (0%)
```

This PR adds the `hugepages-*` entries.

Hi @mattjmcnaughton! 😄 

> What will this display if the user isn't requesting any huge page resources? Will it display 0% usage for all of them?

Yes, that is correct. This is the same behaviour as all the other resource types.


> How many variations of hugepages will it display? Your example shows: ...

It will list all the huge page size resources for the given node. The definition of what is a huge page resource, is defined here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/78915a10949e74feb77586f71ee035292462ea56/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/util/resource/resource.go#L137 (*TL;DR*: Those who starts with `hugepages-`)

This is the same as logic used to find huge page resources in pod specs inside kubelet; https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/78915a10949e74feb77586f71ee035292462ea56/pkg/kubelet/cm/helpers_linux.go#L96

> 3. [...] Are there any concerns about this from a backwards compatibility perspective? [...]

No. This will only use the information previously known in kubectl (no change in the API requests), so there will be no backward compatibility issues.

> Forgive me for my lack of familiarity with hugepages... are these resources automatically included in the cluster?

Yes, that is correct. All huge page sizes supported by the system will be reported to the apiserver by kubelet, including those without any pre allocated pages (capacity `0`). This (the general huge page support) is implemented as specified in the KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/20190129-hugepages.md#node-specification

> In other words, will every use of kubectl start seeing hugepage output when they run kubectl describe node? My concern is that from a usability perspective, that could pollute the contents of the command, especially if most clusters are just reporting 0% of hugepage resources used.

Yes, but I see no point of hiding huge page usage if the capacity is 0, when all other resources are displayed. Today, huge page resources are listed as `capacity`, `allocatable`, but not in `allocated resources`. This only apply to huge pages.

Todays output of `kubectl describe node xyz`

```
[...]
Capacity:
 cpu:                4
 ephemeral-storage:  51343840Ki
 hugepages-1Gi:      0
 hugepages-2Mi:      0
 memory:             8010240Ki
 pods:               110
Allocatable:
 cpu:                4
 ephemeral-storage:  51343840Ki
 hugepages-1Gi:      0
 hugepages-2Mi:      0
 memory:             8010240Ki
 pods:               110
[...]
Allocated resources:
  (Total limits may be over 100 percent, i.e., overcommitted.)
  Resource           Requests    Limits
  --------           --------    ------
  cpu                600m (15%)  100m (2%)
  memory             190Mi (2%)  390Mi (4%)
  ephemeral-storage  0 (0%)      0 (0%)
```

and with this PR:

```
[...]
Capacity:
 cpu:                4
 ephemeral-storage:  51343840Ki
 hugepages-1Gi:      0
 hugepages-2Mi:      0
 memory:             8010240Ki
 pods:               110
Allocatable:
 cpu:                4
 ephemeral-storage:  51343840Ki
 hugepages-1Gi:      0
 hugepages-2Mi:      0

 pods:               110
[...]
Allocated resources:
  (Total limits may be over 100 percent, i.e., overcommitted.)
  Resource           Requests    Limits
  --------           --------    ------
  cpu                600m (15%)  100m (2%)
  memory             190Mi (2%)  390Mi (4%)
  ephemeral-storage  0 (0%)      0 (0%)
  hugepages-1Gi      0 (0%)      0 (0%)
  hugepages-2Mi      0 (0%)      0 (0%)
```
@mattjmcnaughton hugepages are a standard k8s resource, so I think it makes sense to display.  The number of page sizes supported per node varies, so the list will not be huge in practice.

comments: cc @odinuge do you have thoughts here? I see huge pages and think of you :)

Hmm.

Are you sure that there are no other pods using huge page memory @DeepLJH0001 ?
To me, it looks like the node has `36GiB` (huge page @ 1GiB) memory, you are requsting `32GiB`, but `16GiB` is already used.

Can you verify that by listing the pods on the node, and check if some of them are using huge page memory already?

Also, the OS will report that no huge pages are in use as long as no processes have started using the hugepages.

Eg. when a pod requesting `nGiB` with is assigned to a node, k8s will then mark the `nGiB`s with huge page memory it as "used". The cgroup controller (if hugetlb cgroup is mounted) will then set the usage limit to `nGiB`. Before the pod actually starts using the huge page memory, the OS will report that no huge page memory is used. When a process inside the pod maps `nGiB` with huge page memory via eg. `mmap`, the OS will see that the memory is in used.

If the process tries to map more than the requested amount, the map will fail (given that the hugetlb cgroup is mounted).

To verify if the hugetlb cgroup is mounted, run `mount | grep hugetlb`. If mounted, it will retrun something like this:
`hugetlb on /sys/fs/cgroup/hugetlb type cgroup (ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,hugetlb)`
I’m so sorry that there actually has a other pod using hugepage，i only see node info available hugepage. so i close the issue，thanks a lot～
No problem @DeepLJH0001! I think this issue is a symptom that something should be done to make it easier to understand. I will look into it. 😄
